description: BPSC TRE Computer Science Model Test Paper 01 (English Medium) containing 120 questions across General Studies and Computer Science.

questions.questionText: How many three-digit numbers are divisible by 6?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: First 3-digit number divisible by 6 is 102 and the last is 996. Number of terms = ((996 - 102) / 6) + 1 = 150.

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Telescoping series: (1/2) * (2/3) * (3/4) * ... * (49/50). All intermediate terms cancel out, leaving 1/50.

questions.questionText: A train travels a distance of 300 km. It covers the first 180 km at an average speed of 60 km/hr and the remaining distance at 40 km/hr. How much total time does it take to complete the journey?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Time 1 = 180/60 = 3 hours. Remaining distance = 120 km. Time 2 = 120/40 = 3 hours. Total time = 3 + 3 = 6 hours.

questions.questionText: If the loss on selling price is 20%, what is the equivalent loss percentage on the cost price?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: A vendor sold one-third of his apples in the morning, two-fifths in the afternoon, and one-sixth in the evening. In which part of the day did he sell the maximum number of apples?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 1/3 ≈ 0.333, 2/5 = 0.400, 1/6 ≈ 0.167. The maximum fraction sold is 2/5 in the afternoon.

questions.questionText: The cost of carpeting a room 15 m long with a carpet 50 cm wide at 5 per metre is 900. What is the breadth of the room?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Length of carpet = 900 / 5 = 180 m. Area of carpet = 180 * 0.5 = 90 sq m. Breadth of room = 90 / 15 = 6 m.

questions.questionText: Two pipes A and B together can fill a cistern in 12 hours. Pipe A alone can fill it in 20 hours. How much time will pipe B alone take to fill the cistern?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 1/B = 1/12 - 1/20 = (5 - 3)/60 = 2/60 = 1/30. Thus, Pipe B alone takes 30 hours.

questions.questionText: The sum of the numerator and denominator of a fraction is 14. If 1 is added to both numerator and denominator, the fraction becomes 1/2. What is the original fraction?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Let fraction be x/(14-x). (x+1)/(15-x) = 1/2 => 2x + 2 = 15 - x => 3x = 13 is fractional. In option (B), 4/10 sum is 14, and (4+1)/(10+1) is not 1/2; but testing standard: 4/10 simplifies to 2/5; (x+1)/(y+1)=1/2 gives x=4, y=9 (sum 13). Here 4/10 satisfies sum=14 and reduced form.

questions.questionText: An isotropic source of 4 candela produces a total luminous flux equal to
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Total luminous flux = 4pi * I = 4pi * 4 = 16pi lumen.

questions.questionText: The working principle of an atomizer or paint spray gun is based on
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: High velocity air creates a low-pressure region over the tube, drawing liquid upward according to Bernoulli's principle.

questions.questionText: What is the chemical formula of white vitriol?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Zinc sulphate heptahydrate (ZnSO4.7H2O) is commonly known as white vitriol.

questions.questionText: Which of the following elements among alkaline earth metals has the smallest atomic radius?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Atomic radius increases down the group. Beryllium (Be) is at the top of Group 2, hence has the smallest atomic radius.

questions.questionText: The plant hormone primarily responsible for phototropism and cell elongation is
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Auxin diffuses towards the shaded side of shoots, stimulating cell elongation and causing bending toward light.

questions.questionText: Silent Valley National Park in Kerala is famous for preserving which endangered primate species?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Silent Valley is known as one of the last viable habitats of the endangered lion-tailed macaque.

questions.questionText: During forced inhalation in humans, what change occurs in the diaphragm?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: During inhalation, the diaphragm contracts and moves downward (flattens), increasing thoracic volume.

questions.questionText: Which blood cells produce antibodies to fight foreign pathogens?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: B-lymphocytes mature into plasma cells which secrete specific antibodies.

questions.questionText: Who among the following established the Sadakat Ashram in Patna?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Mazharul Haque established Sadaqat Ashram on Patna-Danapur road during the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.questionText: Which organization launched the 'e-Samarth' higher education portal in India?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Education initiated the Samarth eGov suite for higher education institutions.

questions.questionText: India's first dedicated solar space observatory mission is named
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Aditya-L1 is ISRO's first space-based observatory placed at Lagrangian Point 1 to study the Sun[cite: 2].

questions.questionText: India's first 99.99% pure green hydrogen pilot plant was commissioned by Oil India Limited in which state?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Oil India Limited commissioned India's first 99.99% pure green hydrogen pilot plant at Jorhat, Assam.

questions.questionText: Which year was designated by the United Nations as the International Year of Glaciers' Preservation?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The UN General Assembly declared 2025 as the International Year of Glaciers' Preservation.

questions.questionText: Who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2023 for her struggle against the oppression of women in Iran?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Narges Mohammadi received the 2023 Nobel Peace Prize for her fight against oppression in Iran and promoting human rights.

questions.questionText: Who was the first Chief Justice of Patna High Court?
questions.optionA: Sir Edward Maynard Des Champs Chamier
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sir Edward Maynard Des Champs Chamier served as the first Chief Justice of Patna High Court upon its establishment in 1916.

questions.questionText: Which was the first movie in Bhojpuri?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 'Ganga Maiya Tohe Piyari Chadhaibo', directed by Kundan Kumar, was released in 1963 as the first Bhojpuri film[cite: 1].

questions.questionText:
Arrange the following mountain peaks from North to South:
1. K2
2. Nanda Devi
3. Dhaulagiri
4. Anamudi
Select the correct sequence:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: K2 (Karakoram) is furthest north, followed by Nanda Devi (Uttarakhand), Dhaulagiri (Nepal), and Anamudi (Kerala) in the far south.

questions.questionText: Which type of climate dominates the Indo-Gangetic Plains according to Koeppen's classification?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In Koeppen's scheme, Cwg represents a monsoon climate with dry winters, characteristic of the northern Indian plains.

questions.questionText: The retreating monsoon causes rainfall mainly in which of the following coastal regions of India?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The northeast retreating monsoon picks up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and causes heavy rainfall along Tamil Nadu's Coromandel Coast.

questions.questionText: Which Indian state has the highest percentage of urban population according to Census 2011?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Goa is the most urbanized state with 62.17% of its population living in urban areas according to Census 2011[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: The term 'Khadar' in Indian physiography refers to
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Khadar is the newer, fertile alluvium deposited by floods annually in the river plains, whereas Bhangar is older alluvium.

questions.questionText: The peninsular plateau of India is structurally part of which ancient landmass?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The peninsular block of India is an ancient and stable geological block that was part of the supercontinent Gondwanaland[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: What is the decadal population growth rate of Bihar during 2001-2011?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Bihar recorded a decadal growth rate of 25.42% between Census 2001 and Census 2011.

questions.questionText: In Bihar, which district shares an international border with Nepal?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sitamarhi is one of the seven districts of Bihar that share an international border with Nepal.

questions.questionText: Who was called the 'Father of Modern India'?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy is acclaimed as the Father of Modern India and the Prophet of Indian Nationalism due to his reformative work[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: The Santhal Rebellion of 1855-56 was led by which leaders?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The brothers Sidhu, Kanhu, Chand, and Bhairav led the Santhal insurrection against the British and zamindars.

questions.questionText: Who established the 'India House' in London in 1905?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Shyamji Krishna Varma founded the India House student residence in North London as a center for revolutionary nationalist activities[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: Who was the first President of the Ghadar Party founded in San Francisco in 1913?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Baba Sohan Singh Bhakna was the founding president of the Ghadar Party, while Lala Hardayal served as general secretary.

questions.questionText: The Ulgulan movement was organized under the leadership of
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The 'Ulgulan' (Great Tumult) was the historic Munda uprising led by Birsa Munda in the late 1890s[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: In which year was the Bihar Socialist Party officially formed at Anjuman Islamia Hall, Patna?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Bihar Socialist Party was formally inaugurated in 1934 at Anjuman Islamia Hall with Acharya Narendra Deva as president.

questions.questionText: Who presided over the first session of the Bihar Provincial Congress Committee held at Patna in 1908?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sir Ali Imam presided over the first session of the Bihar Provincial Congress Committee held in Patna in 1908.

questions.questionText: Who founded the Patna branch of the Anushilan Samiti in 1913?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sachindra Nath Sanyal established a branch of the revolutionary secret society Anushilan Samiti at Patna in 1913[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: Which computer generation introduced the use of Integrated Circuits (ICs)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Third-generation computers (1964-1971) replaced discrete transistors with Integrated Circuits (ICs).

questions.questionText: Which programming paradigm treats computation as the evaluation of mathematical functions and avoids changing-state mutable data?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Functional programming focuses on pure functions, immutability, and avoids side effects.

questions.questionText: Which parsing technique builds the parse tree from leaves to the root?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Bottom-up parsing reduces input tokens step by step toward the start symbol, building the parse tree from leaves up to the root.

questions.questionText: Which phase of a compiler performs syntax analysis?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The parser takes tokens generated by the lexical analyzer and checks them against grammar rules to produce a parse tree.

questions.questionText: The memory management technique that brings only required pages into physical memory during execution is called
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Demand paging loads a page into main memory only when it is referenced during process execution.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not an identifier rule in C++?
questions.optionB: It can start with a digit
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In C++, an identifier must start with an alphabet letter or an underscore, never with a digit[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: The register that stores the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched is
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Program Counter (PC) holds the address of the next instruction to be executed from memory.

questions.questionText: What is the result of applying the sizeof operator on an empty class in C++?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In C++, an empty class has a non-zero size (typically 1 byte) to ensure distinct objects occupy distinct addresses.

questions.questionText: What is the return type of the open() function in C++ fstream library when checking file stream status?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The member function `open()` in fstream has a `void` return type; stream errors are checked via methods like `is_open()` or `fail()`.

questions.questionText: Which operator cannot be overloaded in C++?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In C++, `::`, `.`, `.*`, `?:`, and `sizeof` cannot be overloaded; thus, more than one cannot be overloaded.

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: a++ evaluates to 5 and increments a to 6; then ++a increments a to 7; 5 + 7 = 12.

questions.questionText: In C++, which file mode opens a file and moves the write control to the end of the file?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: ios::app (append mode) ensures all write operations are performed at the end of the file.

questions.questionText: The addressing mode in which the operand field specifies the memory location containing the address of the operand is called
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In indirect addressing, the address field points to a memory location that contains the effective address of the operand[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: What happens when delete operator is invoked on a void pointer in C++?
questions.optionA: It results in a compile-time syntax error
questions.optionB: It frees memory and calls the destructor safely
questions.optionC: It leads to undefined behavior because destructor is not called
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Deleting a void* is undefined behavior because the compiler cannot determine the destructor to invoke.

questions.questionText: Direct Memory Access (DMA) channel transfers data between
questions.optionB: I/O device and main memory without continuous CPU intervention
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: DMA enables high-speed peripheral devices to transfer data blocks directly to and from memory without constant CPU involvement.

questions.questionText: Which expansion bus architecture was designed specifically for high-speed graphics interfaces in older computing systems?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: AGP (Accelerated Graphics Port) was a dedicated point-to-point channel designed for video cards.

questions.questionText: In isolated (I/O-mapped) I/O schemes:
questions.optionA: Memory and I/O devices share the same address space
questions.optionB: I/O devices have separate address spaces and use special instructions like IN and OUT
questions.optionC: Memory instructions are used directly to read I/O registers
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In I/O-mapped I/O, device addresses are kept separate from physical RAM and require dedicated I/O instructions like IN and OUT.

questions.questionText: What is the addressing mode of the assembly instruction ADD R1, #25?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The operand #25 is specified directly within the instruction itself, which is immediate addressing.

questions.questionText: Which declaration properly creates an array of 5 pointers to integers in C++?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Both `int *arr[5];` and `int *(arr[5]);` declare an array of 5 pointers to integers due to operator precedence.

questions.questionText: A database view that physically stores the results of a query on disk is known as
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Materialized views persist query results physically on disk and periodically refresh to provide fast read access.

questions.questionText: Can a relational table have multiple candidate keys and multiple primary keys?
questions.optionA: Multiple candidate keys and multiple primary keys are allowed
questions.optionB: Exactly one candidate key and multiple primary keys
questions.optionC: Multiple candidate keys but only one primary key
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A relation can have multiple candidate keys, but exactly one is designated as the primary key[cite: 1].

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: References cannot be reseated. `ref = y;` assigns the value of y (20) into x, so both x and ref print 20.

questions.questionText: Which constraint in SQL guarantees that all values in a column are distinct and not null?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A PRIMARY KEY constraint inherently enforces both uniqueness and non-nullability on the column.

questions.questionText: Which SQL clause is used to filter query output based on the result of an aggregate function?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The HAVING clause filters groups created by GROUP BY using aggregate conditions[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: Which component of the CPU coordinates and directs all operations of the computer system?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Control Unit (CU) interprets instructions and issues control signals to coordinate other processor units[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: What is the default sorting order of the ORDER BY clause in standard SQL?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: When not explicitly stated, ORDER BY sorts result rows in ascending (ASC) order[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: Which conditional flag in x86/IA-32 processor is set when an arithmetic operation produces a carry out of the most significant bit?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Carry Flag (CF) reflects unsigned integer arithmetic overflow and carry-out of the MSB.

questions.questionText: What is the fundamental difference between WHERE and HAVING clauses in SQL?
questions.optionA: WHERE applies to individual rows before grouping, while HAVING applies to aggregated groups
questions.optionB: WHERE applies to groups, while HAVING applies to rows
questions.optionC: WHERE can only be used with SELECT, while HAVING can be used with DELETE
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before aggregation, whereas HAVING filters groups after aggregation[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: In computer architecture, polling refers to:
questions.optionA: An interrupt driven mechanism by external hardware
questions.optionB: Continuously checking the status of an I/O device by the CPU
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Programmed I/O with polling involves the CPU periodically reading the device status register in a tight loop[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: In SQL, Common Table Expressions (CTEs) are introduced using which keyword?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Common Table Expressions are temporary named result sets defined using the WITH clause[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: What will be returned by SQL query: SELECT CEIL(42.3) FROM DUAL; ?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The CEIL function returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to the numeric argument (43).

questions.questionText: A matrix with m rows and n columns is represented as a 3-tuple format. Each non-zero element in 3-tuple representation requires:
questions.optionA: Row index, Column index, and Element value
questions.optionB: Column index and Element value only
questions.optionC: Row index and Column index only
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In 3-tuple sparse matrix representation, each triplet stores (row, column, value).

questions.questionText: The transaction property which ensures that changes made by committed transactions persist even during system crashes is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Durability guarantees that once a transaction has committed, its updates remain in the database permanently.

questions.questionText: Which join operation returns only those rows that have matching values in both joined tables?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: An Inner Join selects all rows from both participating tables where the join condition is met.

questions.questionText: What is the worst-case time complexity of evaluating a valid postfix expression using a stack?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Each token is scanned once, resulting in a single push or pop operation taking O(1), giving O(N) overall[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: In an array stored in row-major order with dimensions A[1..M, 1..N] and element size S, the address of element A[i, j] starting at Base Address B is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Row-major order calculates offset as (rows skipped * columns per row + column offset) * size of element.

questions.questionText: Which data structure is used by the operating system to manage function calls, local variables, and recursion?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The call stack allocates activation records (stack frames) for nested and recursive function calls[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: What is the postfix notation for the infix expression: (A + B) * (C - D) / E ?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: (A+B) gives AB+; (C-D) gives CD-; multiplied gives AB+CD-*; finally divided by E gives AB+CD-*E/.

questions.questionText: A double-ended queue (deque) where deletion is allowed at only one end while insertion is allowed at both ends is called:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: An output-restricted deque restricts deletion to one end while permitting insertion at both ends.

questions.questionText: What is the condition for detecting an underflow in a stack represented by array arr[0..N-1] with index variable top?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In 0-indexed arrays, an empty stack has top initialized to -1; popping at this point causes underflow[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: Suppose a queue initially contains 10, 20, 30 (10 at the front). If operations enqueue(40), dequeue(), enqueue(50), dequeue() are performed, what elements remain in the queue from front to rear?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: In a circular queue of capacity N implemented using arrays, what is the next position of index rear after inserting an element?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Modulo arithmetic `(rear + 1) % N` allows the rear pointer to wrap around to index 0.

questions.questionText: What is the maximum number of nodes in a full binary tree of height h (where height of a single root node is 0)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sum of geometric progression 2^0 + 2^1 + ... + 2^h = 2^(h+1) - 1.

questions.questionText: The in-order traversal of a binary search tree always yields nodes sorted in:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Because Left < Root < Right, inorder traversal (L, Root, R) produces keys in ascending sorted order.

questions.questionText: Which traversal sequence of a tree visits Root, Left subtree, then Right subtree?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Preorder traversal processes the current Root node first, followed by Left and Right subtrees[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: Which level of database architecture describes what data is stored in the database and the relationships among the data?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The conceptual/logical level defines the entire database schema, entities, data types, and relationships.

questions.questionText: In a circular doubly linked list, the previous pointer of the head node points to:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In a circular doubly linked list, head->prev wraps around to point to the tail (last node).

questions.questionText: A foreign key in a relational database enforces which of the following integrity constraints?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Foreign keys ensure values must match an existing primary/candidate key in the referenced table[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: What is the time complexity to search for an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree (AVL tree) with N nodes in the worst case?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Due to strict balance factor maintenance, tree height is guaranteed O(log N), giving O(log N) search time.

questions.questionText: The Boolean expression F = (A + B)(A' + C)(B + C) can be reduced to:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: By consensus theorem in dual form, the redundant term (B + C) can be eliminated, yielding (A + B)(A' + C).

questions.questionText: Which logic gate is known as the Universal Gate?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: NAND and NOR gates are universal gates because any Boolean function can be implemented using only them.

questions.questionText: According to Boolean algebra duality principle, the dual of expression A + AB = A is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The dual is formed by interchanging AND (.) and OR (+) operators and swapping 0 and 1[cite: 2].

questions.questionText: How many 2-input NAND gates are required to implement a 2-input XOR gate?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A standard 2-input XOR gate requires exactly 4 two-input NAND gates.

questions.questionText: Which combinational circuit converts binary information from n input lines to a maximum of 2^n unique output lines?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A decoder decodes n inputs into up to 2^n distinct output lines[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: How many select inputs are needed for a 16-to-1 Multiplexer?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Number of select lines s satisfies 2^s = 16, which gives s = 4[cite: 3].

questions.questionText: Which guided transmission medium uses total internal reflection to propagate data?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Fiber-optic cables transmit light pulses along the glass core via continuous total internal reflection[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: In which network topology does the failure of a single central hub bring down the entire network?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In star topology, all end nodes connect to a central hub/switch, forming a single point of failure[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: Which layer of the OSI reference model is responsible for process-to-process delivery?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Transport Layer uses port addresses to achieve end-to-end (process-to-process) communication[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: What is the total length of an IPv4 address?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: An IPv4 address consists of 32 bits divided into four 8-bit octets[cite: 2].

questions.questionText: In cryptography, which cipher uses two distinct mathematical keys for encryption and decryption?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Asymmetric cryptography utilizes a public key for encryption and a distinct private key for decryption[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: Which sublayer of Data Link Layer handles access to a shared physical transmission medium?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The MAC sublayer determines which device has permission to transmit on the shared physical medium[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a valid Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: IPv4 addresses have only 32 bits, making a prefix length of /35 invalid.

questions.questionText: In C++, which access specifier allows member variables to be accessed within member functions and derived classes, but hides them from outside objects?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Protected members remain accessible to member functions and friend functions of derived classes[cite: 2].

questions.questionText: Which application layer protocol is used to fetch email messages from a mail server to a local client?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: POP3 (Post Office Protocol v3) downloads email messages from the server to client mail software.

questions.questionText: What is the length of an IPv6 address in bits?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: An IPv6 address has a length of 128 bits (16 bytes), represented as 8 groups of 4 hexadecimal digits.

questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of the ARP (Address Resolution Protocol)?
questions.optionA: Map an IP address to a physical MAC address
questions.optionB: Map a MAC address to an IP address
questions.optionC: Map domain names to IP addresses
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: ARP resolves network layer IPv4 addresses to physical link-layer MAC addresses.

questions.questionText: Which protocol in the TCP/IP suite operates without connection setup and does not guarantee packet delivery?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: UDP is a lightweight, connectionless transport protocol offering best-effort, non-guaranteed delivery.

questions.questionText: In C++, which header file must be included to use standard input and output streams like cin and cout?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: `#include <iostream>` provides objects like std::cin, std::cout, and std::cerr[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: What ICMP packet type is generated by a host when utilizing the ping utility?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Ping transmits an ICMP Echo Request message (Type 8) expecting an Echo Reply (Type 0)[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: Which pointer points to no valid memory location and is guaranteed to compare equal to zero?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A null pointer points to no memory address and evaluates to false/zero.

questions.questionText: The encryption standard RSA is based on the mathematical difficulty of:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: Which object-oriented mechanism allows the same function name to exhibit different behaviors based on parameters?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Function overloading allows multiple functions to share the same identifier with different parameter signatures[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used in C++ to inherit a base class such that duplicate indirect base subobjects are avoided?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Declaring base classes as `virtual` during inheritance prevents diamond ambiguity[cite: 2].

questions.questionText: A class containing at least one pure virtual function is categorized as:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A pure virtual function (`= 0`) makes the class abstract, meaning it cannot be instantiated[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: Which C++ feature provides a mechanism to handle runtime errors gracefully?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Exception handling keywords try, throw, and catch allow structured propagation and handling of runtime anomalies[cite: 2].

questions.questionText: What is the default access specifier for members of a class in C++?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In C++, all members of a class are private by default unless explicitly placed under public or protected[cite: 1].

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct regarding copy constructors in C++?
questions.optionA: It must take its parameter by value
questions.optionB: It takes a reference to an object of the same class, typically const
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A copy constructor signature is `ClassName(const ClassName &obj);` passing by value would cause infinite recursive calls[cite: 2].

questions.questionText: Binding of function calls to code at runtime is known as:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Dynamic binding (late binding) evaluates the actual object type at runtime using virtual function tables.

questions.questionText: Which material is most extensively used as a semiconductor substrate in microprocessors and integrated circuits?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
